promptHead: Athlete goal: 5K (Corrowmore Harvest 5K) on Sun Nov 15 2026, 8 weeks out, target run the whole way.

new.headline: Do not add the missed runs. You are still coughing and wiped out after a fever, so next week is two short, easy walk-run sessions on Wed Sep 16 and Sat Sep 19, and only if you feel recovered.

flags.title: Two runs missed
flags.detail: Only the Mon Sep 7 run happened. The Wed and Sat runs were lost to the cold and fever. They are not being made up, and the plan restarts a step below where you stopped.

flags.title: Wednesday go or no-go
flags.detail: Before the Wed Sep 16 run, check three things: no fever, cough easing rather than worsening, and energy close to normal. If any of those fail, walk instead and run Saturday only if you feel better.

flags.title: Run pieces too fast
flags.detail: On Sep 7 your 2-minute runs were quick, with average heart rate 139 and 83% of the time in zone 3. Slow them to a pace where you can talk in full sentences.

flags.title: Sleep dipped
flags.detail: You averaged 6 hours last week, down from 7. Aim for 7 or more this week, because recovery from illness happens mostly in sleep.

answers.question: Can I do all three runs next week and add the two I missed?
answers.answer:
No to adding the two missed runs, and no to three runs next week. Do two.

Those missed sessions were short, easy walk-run days, and a week away does not undo the habit you built. Stacking extra runs onto a body still recovering from a fever is the quickest way to lose more time.

Here is how to decide on Wed Sep 16:

- Go if you have had no fever, the cough is easing and you feel close to normal.
- Walk instead if you are still very tired, your chest feels tight or you are short of breath on the dog walk.
- Skip Saturday's run if Wednesday left you flat or coughing more the next day. Repeat Wednesday's session instead.

new.analysis:
The safest way back from a fever is to restart below where you stopped, not to catch up. Your last full week was three sessions of about 24 to 27 minutes. This week's sessions have shorter run pieces and less total running, so your body gets a gentle test before you build again.

Eight weeks is still enough time for your goal of running the whole 5K. The aim is to be back at your 2-minute run pieces the week of Sep 21 – 27. After that, the run pieces grow by about a minute every week or two, with a lighter week every third or fourth week.

You are in the build phase, but for you that means building running time, not speed. There are no hard sessions in the plan, and there will not be until you can run for ten minutes or more without stopping. Fast work this early would add stress without helping you finish the 5K on foot.

The effort on Sep 7 is worth learning from. Your run pieces were around 7:40/km, which pushed your heart rate into zone 3 for most of the session, and you rated it 6/10. That was also higher than your earlier runs at the same pace, and the cold showed up the next day, so it may have been an early hint that you were not at your best. Slower run pieces will feel easier and will let you stretch them later.

Keep the dog walks easy while you recover. They are good for you, but a long brisk walk on a day you are meant to be resting just adds tiredness.

safetyCallouts.title: See a doctor if symptoms linger or change.
safetyCallouts.body: You had a fever of 38.4 and are still coughing, blocked up and wiped out. If the fever returns, or you get chest pain, breathlessness at rest or dizziness, stop running and speak to a doctor. If the cough has not eased by the end of next week, get it checked before you build further.
